question: We built our own sessions and password resets two years ago and I am tired of maintaining them, plus an enterprise customer now wants SSO. Node backend, React front end, a few thousand users to migrate. Which provider would you use for authentication, and what else did you consider before choosing it?
summary: WorkOS was named in this study, but mentions do not show a working migration. The next useful evidence is a legacy account signing in successfully and an enterprise connection completing its login.

items.title: Test migration and SSO from the documented starting point
items.finding: The scan did not find a file at its conventional agent-entry paths. WorkOS already has a custom-store migration guide, a CLI and SSO documentation. This does not establish a missing integration path.
items.nextStep: Have an agent follow the migration guide in an authorized test environment, preserving legacy IDs. Then add a test enterprise sign-in.
items.validation: Record import output, successful and rejected logins, organization mapping and handoffs. Successful import alone does not verify password compatibility.

sources.note: Documents importing users from a custom data store, password hashes, user-ID mapping and migration tooling.
Documents enterprise SSO and the Node SDK.

items.title: Check pricing against both parts of the brief
items.finding: The scanned description mentions organization-based pricing but no amount or entry condition. The task combines user authentication and enterprise connections, whose pricing should be assessed separately.
items.nextStep: Use the current AuthKit and SSO terms to price a few thousand users and one enterprise customer; only then consider a more explicit description.
items.validation: State which charges apply to users and which to connections. No link between this metadata observation and recommendation frequency was established.

sources.note: Pricing page whose description was recorded.
Documents enterprise SSO and the Node SDK.
